evidence.field: 說文解字 and 說文解字注
evidence.text: The Shuowen entry defines 買 as 市 and analyzes it as 从网貝 (net + cowrie/money shell), citing the Mencius phrase about using a raised position to monopolize market profit. The later Shuowen commentary explicitly calls the structure 會意. This is an early lexicographic analysis, not independent proof of the graph’s original motivation.
evidence.title: 買 mǎi - 汉典

evidence.field: 康熙字典; cited classical text examples
evidence.text: The page reports the older graph 𧵽 in its Shuowen quotation and cites 周禮·天官·小宰, 聽賣買以質劑, and 前漢·食貨志, 衆民賣買五穀、布帛、絲緜之物. These attest the buy/sell usage in texts attributed to the Zhou ritual text and the Former Han history, but the accessed page does not establish the date of the surviving witnesses or the precise date of the wording.
evidence.title: 買 mǎi - 汉典

evidence.source: 教育局中國語文教育研究及評估組資源：字源考釋
evidence.text: This source says the oracle, bronze and seal forms contain net and 貝 as semantic elements and interprets the graph as using a net to obtain cowries, which served as ancient currency; it gives the basic sense as exchanging money for goods. Its wording is a traditional graphic interpretation; its displayed paleographic forms were not visually inspected here.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 買

evidence.field: 國語辭典 and cited literary examples
evidence.text: The dictionary separates purchasing goods from an extended sense 求取 (‘seek/obtain’), citing Tang poems by Bai Juyi and Liu Hun for purchase, and the 南史 passage and Song Su Shi poem for seeking fame or favor. These examples document later literary uses; they do not date the semantic extension’s origin.
evidence.title: 買 mǎi - 汉典

evidence.text: The page reports the competing analysis that 買 is phonosemantic: abbreviated phonetic 羅 (*rˤaj) plus semantic 貝. This differs from Shuowen’s explicit net-plus-cowrie 会意 analysis. The accessible material does not provide Baxter and Sagart’s character-specific argument; therefore the phonetic analysis is recorded as an attributed proposal, not established fact.
evidence.title: 買 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: For 買 the page gives Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *mˤrajʔ, Middle Chinese meaX, and modern Beijing Mandarin mǎi; it separately gives Zhengzhang Old Chinese *mreːʔ. These are system-specific reconstructions and must not be merged. The local Baxter–Sagart row for 買 agrees: meaX, *mˤrajʔ, GSR 1240c (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, row 2225). No matching local 羅 row was verified in this search, so the comparative pronunciation of the proposed phonetic component was not independently checked here.
evidence.title: 買 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Sagart, Laurent; The Hmong-Mien rice vocabulary borrowed into Chinese? (Springer article)
evidence.field: Section Hmong-Mien rice vocabulary borrowed into Chinese?
evidence.text: The article reports Haudricourt and Strecker’s proposal that 買 ‘buy’ and 賣 ‘sell’ were borrowed from Hmong-Mien, then states that Sagart (1995) argued the direction was Chinese into Hmong-Mien. This challenges the Hmong-Mien-to-Chinese direction but does not decide the wider Chinese–Hmong-Mien relationship. Wiktionary’s summary additionally reports Ratliff’s three-way alternatives (borrowing either way or common inheritance) and that more evidence is needed; that latter summary was not verified against Ratliff’s original work.
evidence.title: How Many Independent Rice Vocabularies in Asia?

evidence.text: Unicode describes Unihan as a database of Han-character properties, including readings and definitions, with readings varying across place and time. Its official individual lookup URLs for U+8CB7 and U+4E70 were attempted but inaccessible through the web tool. Local data inspected: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt rows 173908 (U+8CB7 kMandarin mǎi) and 31019 (U+4E70 kMandarin mǎi); local HSK extract pipeline/data/unihan-kmandarin-hsk1.tsv row 25 records U+4E70 kMandarin mǎi. The upstream official Annex explains Unihan generally but does not itself verify these character-specific values.
evidence.title: UAX #38: Unicode Han Database (Unihan)

evidence.text: The inspected data line is U+4E70 买 kTraditionalVariant U+8CB7. It verifies the simplified/traditional variant mapping in Unicode’s database. It establishes a variant mapping, not a cursive derivation history.
evidence.title: unihan-database/kTraditionalVariant.txt

gaps: No independently verified oracle-bone or bronze specimen and dated context was inspected; Han Dian lists Shang oracle and bronze examples, including 商代晚期 vessels, but its displayed glyph images were not viewed. Claims about earliest attestation and precise graphic transitions remain unresolved.
The derivation of the graph’s net element as a depiction of a net capturing cowries is a traditional explanation, not independently established here; the graph’s original motivation could differ.

The phonetic-compound account is attributed to Baxter–Sagart by secondary pages. The actual character-specific discussion and the component 羅’s pronunciation/readings were not verified from primary Baxter–Sagart material. Local Baxter–Sagart data confirmed only 買’s row; do not treat it as evidence for 羅’s proposed sound role.

Official Unicode character-specific lookup pages were attempted for both U+8CB7 and U+4E70 but the web tool returned inaccessible errors. Character-specific current readings are supported by inspected local Unihan rows, but no verified official character-page click-through evidence was obtained.

The word’s earliest securely dated attestation and the chronology among senses ‘market/trade’, ‘buy’, ‘obtain/seek’, ‘bribe’ and ‘persuade’ remain undetermined. Gloss order and later dictionary examples do not establish semantic chronology.

The deeper lexical proposals involving Proto-Sino-Tibetan, Austro-Tai and Hmong-Mien remain disputed or secondary-summary claims; this pass verified only the reported debate about Hmong-Mien borrowing direction, not the original comparative datasets.

The local full Unihan readings file contains both characters’ Mandarin rows (買 U+8CB7 mǎi; 买 U+4E70 mǎi), while the tracked HSK extract contains only 买. These are repository data, not character-specific external citations. No small local extract is recommended: the record use here is limited and the Unicode database licensing/reuse terms for such an extract were not verified.
